theory.intro: When $X$ is replaced by $aX+b$, the mean changes in the same way: $E(aX+b)=aE(X)+b$.
facts: $E(aX+b)=aE(X)+b$: multiply the mean by $a$, then add $b$.
Adding $b$ shifts every value equally, so it moves the centre.
This rule needs only $E(X)$, not the whole distribution.
steps: Write the new variable in the form $aX+b$ and read off $a$ and $b$.

workedExamples.solution_text:
(a)
$\begin{aligned} E(4X+3)&=4E(X)+3\\&=4(6.5)+3\\&=29 \end{aligned}$

(b) The coefficient of $X$ is $-2$.
$\begin{aligned} E(9-2X)&=-2E(X)+9\\&=-2(6.5)+9\\&=-4 \end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text:
A game's net gain $X$, in dollars, has $E(X)=-0.8$. The operator doubles the player's net gain and then charges an extra $\$0.60$, giving $Y=2X-0.6$.
Find $E(Y)$ and explain whether the change helps the player.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned} E(Y)&=2E(X)-0.6\\&=2(-0.8)-0.6\\&=-2.2 \end{aligned}$

The expected net gain is $-\$2.20$ per play. The expected loss increases from $\$0.80$ to $\$2.20$, so the change does not help the player.

workedExamples.question_text:
The discrete random variable $X$ has the following distribution.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc} x&0&2&5\\\hline P(X=x)&0.2&0.5&0.3 \end{array}$
Find $E(3X-4)$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
First multiply each outcome by its probability and add.
$\begin{aligned} E(X)&=0(0.2)+2(0.5)+5(0.3)\\&=0+1+1.5\\&=2.5 \end{aligned}$

Apply the linearity rule.
$\begin{aligned} E(3X-4)&=3E(X)-4\\&=3(2.5)-4\\&=3.5 \end{aligned}$

foundation.question_text:
Raw test marks $X$ have mean $58$.
The marks are scaled using $Y=1.2X+5$.
Find the mean scaled mark.

development.question_text:
The daily maximum temperature $X$, in degrees Celsius, has $E(X)=21.5$.
The temperature in degrees Fahrenheit is $F=1.8X+32$.
Find $E(F)$.

A worker's weekly overtime hours $H$ have $E(H)=4.2$.
Weekly pay in dollars is $W=920+45H$.
Find $E(W)$, correct to the nearest cent.

A game's net gain $X$ in dollars has $E(X)=-0.5$.
The operator triples the player's net gain and then charges an extra $\$1$, so the new net gain is $Y=3X-1$.
Find $E(Y)$, and state whether the change helps the player.
mastery.solution_text:
$E(Y)=3(-0.5)-1$
$=-1.5-1$
$=-\$2.50$
The expected loss per play grows from $\$0.50$ to $\$2.50$, so the change does not help the player.
